picks.file: Atlas Beudeker-C9E10 040 12X-TRAIECTUM ad Mosam, urbs et natura loci, munitionibusq. et populi frequetia, et edificijs, et Ampliss- ....jpeg
picks.what: Panorama across the Maas, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 2 (British Library)
picks.who: Georg Braun and Frans Hogenberg, after Simon de Bellomonte
picks.why: true panorama of the walled town beyond the river with St. Servatius and the other church towers; coat-of-arms cartouche and text panels trimmed

picks.what: View from the Aachen side, engraving (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: general view of the skyline with St. John’s tower over the fields; margins and caption trimmed

picks.file: Panorama Maastricht vanaf Fort St Pieter, ca 1804.jpg
picks.what: Panorama from Fort Sint Pieter, colored drawing
picks.why: color general view from the fortress hill with St. Servatius and St. John’s towers; paper edges trimmed

picks.file: Maastricht, panorama vanuit het westen (Ph v Gulpen, ca 1845).jpg
picks.what: Panorama from the western city wall, colored drawing (Historisch Centrum Limburg)
picks.why: color panorama over roofs and gardens to the towers of St. Servatius and St. John’s; legend strip at left trimmed; 41 years after #15

picks.file: NIMH - 2011 - 0321 - Aerial photograph of Maastricht, The Netherlands - 1920 - 1940.jpg
picks.what: Aerial photograph (Netherlands Institute of Military History)
picks.why: the Maas with the old St. Servatius Bridge and the Wilhelmina Bridge between the center and Wyck; negative edges and scratches trimmed

gaps: P0: nothing (#1 is a Nuremberg Chronicle bridge-collapse scene, not a town view); P4: nothing strong; P6: only close-up street photos, no skyline or center view
notes: #4 is dated to vol. 2 (1575), as the BnF copy (#5) is described; the British Library record gives 1572. #5 is the same panorama with modern white highlighting. #2, #3, #6, #7 and #8 are town plans. P4 alternatives: #17 (Schaepkens, the western wall in snow, about 1865, color) and #21 (1890 etching of the Maas at night, very dark). #18–20 are 1900s photos of van der Meulen’s 1672 siege drawings. #10 (pen drawing, dated only “ca. 1740?”) left out for the uncertain date.
